threads.thread_goal: Agree on the process for creating the facility layout plan.

messages.text: Team, let's kick off the planning for the new production line facility. The main priority is getting an approved layout and fit-out plan. Given the 30-day deadline for the pilot batch, we need to move quickly. I've attached the leased space floor plan (A1). We'll also need a consolidated equipment list (A2) to inform the layout. @48820 @49409 @255537 @518065 what are your initial thoughts on the process?

Thanks for starting this. Before we get too deep into the layout, I'll review the lease agreement for any clauses on structural alterations, HVAC modifications, or waste disposal requirements. That could impact where we can place certain equipment.

I can go to the site tomorrow morning. I need to check the actual locations of power mains, water hookups, and ventilation ducts. The floor plan (A1) is good, but we need to verify what's physically there before we decide where a machine goes.

Good point on the equipment list (A2). We need to factor in not just the production machines but also the quality control station. It requires specialized lighting, ventilation for material fumes, and an anti-static environment. Its placement is critical and can't be an afterthought.
I agree. I will start thinking about the process flow from raw material intake to the final product packaging. We should try to make the flow logical to avoid issues later.

Excellent points all around. Let's formalize this. @255537, your on-site survey is the perfect first step, let's track that as T1. @518065, great catch on the lease, please proceed. @49409 and @48820, please collaborate to produce a final equipment requirements list, including those QC details. We'll call that T2. Once we have the survey results and the equipment list, I can draft the initial layout plan, which we'll call A3.
To confirm the decisions here: I will lead the creation of the layout plan (A3) once inputs are ready (D1). The immediate first step is the technical site survey (T1) (D2).

threads.thread_goal: Establish the quality criteria for the pilot batch.

messages.text: Hi @48820, to build on our discussion about the QC station, we should define the quality standards for the pilot batch now. This will impact the 'End-to-end production process and quality control workflow' deliverable. I've started a draft document (A4). I propose we align our criteria with the ISO 13485 standard for medical devices as a baseline. It's the most relevant framework for these types of appliances.
Yes, quality is very important. ISO 13485 is a good starting point. What specific tests and checks do you think we need to include in our workflow?

For these appliances, the critical-to-quality characteristics are dimensional accuracy to the micron, material purity to avoid contamination, and surface finish. I can draft an initial QC checklist (A5) detailing the specific parameters, measurement methods, and pass/fail tolerances for each. I should have a first draft ready for you to look at by tomorrow.
Ok, that sounds like a good plan. Please send over the draft checklist (A5) when it's ready and I will review it against our planned production process.

Perfect. So, we are aligned. Decision: The quality criteria will be based on ISO 13485 standards (D3). And I will draft the initial QC checklist (A5) for the pilot batch (D4). I'll create T3 for this.

threads.thread_goal: Align on scope and target operating model for centralised management.

messages.text: Team, welcome to the official channel for the 'Launch of Centralised Residential Property Management Model' project. The goal is to streamline our operations to improve efficiency and tenant satisfaction. First step is to align on the scope and operating model. I've attached the initial brief. Please review and share your thoughts on which properties we should include in the first wave.

Thanks. I've already started mapping our current processes for T1. Based on that, I suggest we start with the 'Maple View' and 'Oak Residence' buildings. They have a good mix of unit types and their current processes are the most inconsistent, so we'll see the biggest impact there. I've put some initial thoughts into a draft operating model, A1, which outlines how centralisation could work.

Maple View is good, but Oak Residence has that big plumbing job next month. Maybe 'Willow Creek' instead? It's newer and the tenants are easier to deal with. I can get the unit inventory done for any of them pretty fast.
Where can I find the brief document?

It's in the project folder, I'll send you the link directly. @167424 good point on the plumbing, but the goal is to test the model under realistic conditions. A planned maintenance event is a perfect test for our new processes.

I've reviewed A1. The model seems sound, but we need to consider the different legal entities that own the various buildings. Maple View is under 'Property Corp A' while Oak Residence is 'Portfolio B'. This will have implications for the rental agreements and owner reporting. We should probably start with buildings under a single ownership structure to simplify the initial rollout.
Excellent point, @128593. That's a critical dependency. Let's adjust the scope. @48703 can you propose two buildings under the same entity? Let's stick to 'Property Corp A' for now.
Understood. In that case, let's go with 'Maple View' and 'Cedar Point'. Both are under 'Property Corp A' and have a similar tenant profile. I'll update the scope notes.
Cedar Point is fine. No big jobs planned there.

Perfect. Let's lock that in. Decision: The first rollout wave will include 'Maple View' and 'Cedar Point'. Now, regarding the operating model in A1. Any major concerns with the proposed responsibilities matrix for T2?

The RACI in A1 looks mostly correct for leasing and billing. However, for legal escalations, the 'Consulted' role should include our external legal counsel, not just an internal review. I'll add a note in the document.
I agree with @128593. I've also clarified the handover points between the central team and the on-site staff for maintenance requests. I think it's ready for approval from my side.
It looks ok to me.
Good catch. Please make that change. With that amendment, I'm happy to approve the model. Decision: The draft centralised operating model in A1 is approved, pending the legal counsel clarification.
Great. I'll continue with the detailed process mapping for T1 based on this approved model. I'll have the first draft maps for Maple View ready by EOD tomorrow.
Excellent progress. Let's keep the momentum going.
So I should focus on getting the inventory for Maple View and Cedar Point first? I can start that now.
Yes, please prioritize those two. Let me know if you find any urgent maintenance issues.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise tenant lifecycle documents and checklists.

messages.text: Hi all, here is the first draft of the tenant onboarding checklist A2 for T3. Please let me know your thoughts.

Thanks @52814. I've taken a look. We need to add sections for meter readings (gas, water, electric) and a confirmation that the tenant has received the welcome pack with emergency contact info. Also, a line for 'photographic record of property condition' is essential to prevent deposit disputes later.
Taking photos of every room will take a lot of time during changeover. Can we just do the kitchen and bathroom?

Unfortunately, partial records won't hold up well. We need photos of all rooms, including floors, walls, and any existing fixtures. It's a critical step for compliance and financial protection. We can create a simple shot list to make it faster for the on-site team. Also, looking at A2, we must include a check for the energy performance certificate (EPC) being provided, as that's a legal requirement.
Good point on the EPC, I missed that. @52814 please add all these points to the next version of A2. @167424 we'll make a simple guide for the photos to make it efficient.
Ok I will update it. What about the rental agreement? Is that ready?

I'm working on the updated rental agreement templates for T4. The main draft is complete, but I'm waiting for the final compliance review on a new clause regarding shared facilities usage. I've uploaded the current draft to the A3 folder for review. It incorporates the latest tenancy deposit scheme rules.
Team, good discussion. Let's finalize the checklist. @52814 please share the updated A2 with the additions from @48703 and @128593. Once we see that, we can approve it.
Here is the updated version of A2.
This looks comprehensive now. It covers all the key stages. I'm happy with this.
Great. Decision: The content and structure of the tenant onboarding checklist A2 are approved. Let's move to the rental agreement. @128593 when do you expect the final compliance review on A3?
I just heard back. The legal review is complete and the feedback is minor. I've incorporated the changes into A3. It's ready for use in the pilot.
Excellent. Decision: The updated rental agreement templates in A3 are approved for use in the pilot. This concludes the core tenant lifecycle documents. Well done team.
Now that these are approved, @52814 can you start drafting the tenant-facing FAQ for T9? It should cover the main points from A2 and A3.
Yes, I will start on T9.
Ok, I understand about the photos. A guide would be helpful.
I'll draft a one-page guide for you and the other on-site staff by tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Plan maintenance, inspections and compliance activities.

messages.text: Hi team, I've created an initial proposal for the Maintenance and Inspection Master Schedule, A5, as part of T6. It outlines preventive maintenance tasks and inspection frequencies. I'd appreciate your feedback, especially from @167424 on feasibility and @128593 on regulatory alignment.

I looked at A5. The quarterly fire alarm test is fine, but doing a full HVAC service twice a year on the older buildings seems like a lot. We usually only do it once. Also, the inventory for T5 is ongoing, I found some damp in unit 2B at Maple View, I put it in the sheet A4.

Thanks for the flag on 2B, I'll schedule a specialist to look at it. Regarding the HVAC, the bi-annual service is a new requirement for the energy efficiency certification we're targeting. We need to stick to that frequency.

The schedule in A5 looks solid for safety compliance. However, we should categorize buildings by age and construction type. A 1970s block will have different inspection needs for things like wiring and insulation compared to a modern build. We should define at least two building categories with slightly different scopes for the annual deep-dive inspection.

That's a great idea. It makes the plan more robust and efficient. I'll create two categories: 'Pre-2000' and 'Post-2000'. For the 'Pre-2000' buildings, I'll add a mandatory electrical wiring check every two years. Does that sound right?

Yes, that aligns with best practice and upcoming regulatory guidance. Let's formalize that. Decision: Inspection frequency and scope in A5 will be set based on two building categories, 'Pre-2000' and 'Post-2000', with specific checks for each.
Who will be doing the inspections?
@167424 and the on-site team will handle routine checks. Specialist inspections like gas safety and electrical will be done by certified external contractors. It's all in the operating model A1.
Ok, I can handle the different checks if I have a clear list. I'm working on the compliance checklist for T12 now. It has fire safety and access stuff. Is that what you mean?

Exactly. That checklist from T12 is critical. We need to ensure every item on it is non-negotiable and checked during the scheduled inspections for all buildings, regardless of age. Let's make that an official decision.
I agree. Compliance is not optional. Decision: The compliance checklist items defined in T12 are confirmed as mandatory for all buildings during their scheduled inspections.
Great. I'll finalize A5 with these decisions incorporated. @167424 please share the draft of the T12 checklist when you have it so I can align the schedule timings.
Will send it over tomorrow morning.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on KPIs, dashboard structure and reporting cadence.

messages.text: Hello, as part of T7 I have created a first version of the property performance dashboard template A6. It includes occupancy and open issues. What other metrics should we add?
Thanks. This is a start, but we need more financial and operational depth. I want to see rent arrears as a percentage of total rent roll, and average time to resolve maintenance requests.

Agree with @54175. I'd also add 'percentage of scheduled inspections completed on time' and 'tenant satisfaction score' once we have a survey method. For now, we can use 'number of formal complaints' as a proxy.
From a portfolio perspective, we should also track 'average void period' between tenancies and 'lease renewal rate'. These are leading indicators of portfolio health and desirability.
Ok, so I should add: arrears, time to resolve, inspections completed, complaints, void period, and renewal rate?

Yes, that's a much stronger set of KPIs. Let's formalize this. Decision: The final set of KPIs to track in dashboard A6 will be: Occupancy, Rent Arrears, Avg. Time to Resolve Maintenance, Inspections Completed, Formal Complaints, Avg. Void Period, and Lease Renewal Rate.
That works. We'll need to ensure the on-site teams are logging the data correctly, especially for maintenance resolution times. I'll add that to their training.
What do I need to do for this? Just close the tickets when the job is done?
Yes, exactly. Log the issue when you get it, and close it immediately when it's resolved. The system will calculate the time automatically.
Now for the cadence. I want to see a summary of this dashboard weekly. For property owners, a more concise version should be sent monthly. This will be part of the owner communication pack T8.
Weekly for senior management and monthly for owners sounds right. It gives us time to act on trends internally before they become owner concerns.
Agreed. Let's lock that in. Decision: Performance reports will be shared weekly with senior management and monthly with property owners.
I will update A6 with the final KPIs and add a note about the reporting schedule.

threads.thread_goal: Prepare pilot rollout, communication and incident handling approach.

messages.text: Okay team, time to plan the pilot for T10. Based on our earlier decision, I propose we officially select 'Maple View' and 'Cedar Point'. I've checked the upcoming schedule, and a good start date would be the 1st of next month. This gives us time to prep the comms. I've also attached a draft of the owner and tenant communication pack A7.
Sounds good. The inventory in A4 for both buildings is almost complete. Just a heads up, Cedar Point has a few tenants who complain about everything. We should be ready for that.

That's actually a good thing for a pilot. It will be a robust test of our new incident and escalation procedure. Speaking of which, I've drafted the procedure for T11 and uploaded it as A8. It defines severity levels and response times. We need to make sure the on-site team is comfortable with it.

Thanks @128593, I'll review A8 with @167424 this afternoon. The comms pack A7 looks good, but I think the owner FAQ needs a clearer point on how they can escalate issues if they're not happy with the new model. @54175 this is related to your work on T8.

Good point. I'll add a section to the owner comms in A7 clarifying the new service levels and the single point of contact for escalations. Let's get these documents finalized. Are there any other concerns with the pilot buildings or start date?
Who is sending the communications to the tenants?
The central housing team will send the initial email, and the on-site staff will post notices in the common areas. It's detailed in the comms plan within A7.
Hearing no objections, let's make the call. Decision: The pilot will start on the 1st of next month in 'Maple View' and 'Cedar Point'.
I've reviewed the comms pack A7. The language is clear and addresses the key risks like tenant resistance. The incident procedure A8 is also solid. I think they're ready.
Great. I've reviewed A8 with @167424 and he understands the new logging process. And @54175 has added the escalation point to A7. I believe both documents are ready for approval.
Excellent. Decision: The owner and tenant communication pack A7 and the incident procedure A8 are approved for use in the pilot.
Perfect. I'll kick off the pre-pilot checklist and schedule the comms send-out. We are on track for T10.
Yes, I know what to do for incidents now. Log it in the system right away.

threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, objectives, and roles before detailed planning starts.

messages.text: Hello team, welcome to the official channel for the Integrated Youth Wellbeing and Outreach Pilot Programme. To kick things off, please review the Pilot Programme Overview (A1). The goal for this week is to align on our scope and roles so we can move into detailed planning.
Thanks for setting this up. I've read through A1. It looks like a solid plan. I'm ready to start on the templates and formatting tasks whenever the content is ready.

Hi all. I've started thinking about T1, mapping the youth groups. I have a few places in mind, like the Northwood Community Centre and the Parkside estate. Are these the kinds of locations we're looking for?

That's a good start, @1424. For T6, it would be helpful to get a full list of potential locations. Once we have that, I can create a map (A6) to visualize the area and plan the most efficient routes between them. We should also consider which schools we'll be partnering with.

Exactly. @1424, let's aim to finalize a list of 3-4 priority locations and 2 partner schools this week. That will be our first key decision (D1). Please check with the social services manager for their input as well.
Hello. For the oral health part, T5, will I be working alone or with someone else during the sessions?

Good question, @98920. The plan is for you to lead the oral health sessions, but a youth or pastoral worker will always be present to support with group management and any safeguarding concerns. This brings us to our second key decision: clarifying roles (D2).
Ok, I will talk to the manager. So for D1, the list should be final by Friday? I'll add the two secondary schools we usually work with.
I can create a simple roles and responsibilities chart based on the backlog and our discussion here. It can be a reference for everyone.

That would be very helpful, thank you @61769. Let's formalize the roles then (D2): I'll take the lead on the workshop curriculum and safeguarding procedures. @1424 will lead on outreach and youth engagement. @98920 will lead the oral health sessions. @522004 will manage the field schedule and data analysis support. @61769 will support with documentation and materials. Does everyone agree with this division of responsibilities?
Works for me. Once @1424 has the locations for T1 confirmed, I'll get started on T6.
Yes, that is clear. Thank you.
Sounds good.
Confirmed.

Update: I've spoken with the manager. The confirmed locations are: Northwood Community Centre, Parkside Youth Club, and the public library. The partner schools are Eastside Secondary and Parkside Academy. I'll put this in a doc.

Excellent. That settles it. Decision D1 is confirmed: we will target those three locations and two schools for the pilot. Decision D2 on roles is also confirmed as per my message above. Great progress, everyone.
Perfect. I have what I need to start on the draft schedule for T6.
I've created the R&R chart and shared the link in the channel header.

threads.thread_goal: Define safeguarding, confidentiality, and record-keeping standards.

messages.text: Hi all, as part of T2, I've drafted the Safeguarding and Confidentiality Procedures (A2). The document is now in the project folder for your review. Please pay close attention to the sections on consent and data handling. All feedback is welcome.

Thanks, I'm on it. This connects directly to T4 and the data collection templates (A3). A key question for us to decide (D4) is what the absolute minimum data fields are that we need to record for each interaction. Simpler is better for compliance and workload.
I'm reading through A2 now. For T8, the record-keeping system, will we need a separate folder for each young person? Or one big file? I'm worried about keeping track of everything.

Good question, @1424. The procedures in A2 recommend a secure digital folder for each individual receiving one-to-one support to maintain confidentiality. For general attendance at workshops, a single, anonymised list per session is sufficient. Let's make sure that's clear.

Regarding D4, I agree with keeping it simple. For evaluation purposes, we need a unique (but anonymised) ID, the date, the type of activity, and the location. This allows us to track engagement patterns without collecting unnecessary personal data.
In the dental clinic we have very strict rules for patient information. Will these procedures in A2 be enough? I need to be sure before I start.

A very important point, @98920. This draft is based on social care standards. I've included a note that all health-related information must also adhere to clinical confidentiality guidelines. Before we finalize, I will share A2 with the dental clinic supervisor and the compliance officer for their formal sign-off.
Ok, that makes sense. So for T8 I will plan for individual folders for the one-to-one support cases.
So for the minimum data fields (D4), are we agreeing on: Anonymised ID, Date, Activity Type, Location? I can build the template in A3 around that right away.
Yes, let's confirm that. Decision D4: The minimum data fields for all interactions will be Anonymised ID, Date, Activity Type, and Location. Any objections?
None from me. That's a solid foundation.
Agreed.
Great, I'll proceed with the templates (A3) based on this.

Perfect. I'll incorporate the feedback into A2 and send it for final review. Assuming no major issues are raised by the external stakeholders, we can consider the procedures approved by tomorrow EOD. That will close out decision D3.
Quick update: The compliance officer and dental supervisor have both approved the procedures in A2. We are now formally approved. Decision D3 is made.
That is good news. I feel more comfortable now.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise workshop curriculum and oral health session design.

messages.text: Team, I've uploaded the first draft of the Youth Wellbeing Workshop Curriculum Pack (A4) for T3. It outlines 8 potential session topics. I'd appreciate your thoughts on the flow and content.
At the same time, I have put together a draft protocol for the Oral Health sessions (A5) as part of T5. It includes the main talking points and a list of materials I think we will need.
Looking at A4, the topics seem good. Maybe we could do the 'stress management' one earlier? A lot of the young people I talk to are worried about exams.

That's a great suggestion, @1424. We can definitely be flexible with the order. Let's tentatively agree to move 'Stress Management' to week 2. If everyone is happy with the general topics, we can get approval for the initial set (D5).
The curriculum in A4 looks very comprehensive. Once the topics are locked in (D5), I can start formatting the handouts and materials for each session.

I've reviewed the oral health protocol in A5. It seems practical. @98920, have you considered the time constraints? The schedule will be tight, so we need to be sure the activities are feasible (D6). A 15-minute talk plus a 5-minute screening per person could take a long time for a large group.
That is a good point. Maybe the screening is not for everyone. We could do the talk for the whole group and then offer the screening only to those who are interested and have questions?

That sounds like a very sensible adjustment, @98920. It keeps the activity manageable and respects the young people's choice. Let's decide on that approach. Decision D6: The oral health sessions will consist of a group awareness talk, followed by optional, one-to-one screenings for interested participants. This seems feasible.
Ok, I will update the protocol in A5. I also need to work on T11, the inventory checklist. I will use the materials list from A5 to create the checklist (A7).
I'm happy with the workshop topics in A4.
The topics look relevant and well-structured. No objections from me.

Great. With that, we have consensus. Decision D5 is confirmed: The initial set of 8 wellbeing workshop topics is approved, with 'Stress Management' moved to week 2. I will now get formal approval from the social services manager.
Excellent. I'll start preparing the materials for the first two workshops then.
I have created the first version of the materials checklist A7 for T11. It is in the folder.
Thank you @98920. That's very efficient.
The optional screening sounds much better for engagement.
Agreed, that's a practical solution.
Makes sense.
Okay, we have full agreement on both points. This thread is complete.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on field visit schedule, logistics, and coordination with schools.

messages.text: Hi team, following on from T1, I've completed a draft Field Visit Schedule and Location Map (A6) for T6. Please review and let me know if there are any immediate conflicts or issues. The goal is to lock this in (D7) by the end of the week.

Thanks for this. Looking at the schedule, Tuesday afternoon at Parkside Youth Club might be difficult. They have a sports program then and it gets very loud. Maybe we could switch it with the library visit on Wednesday?
Good local knowledge, thanks @1424. That's an easy swap to make. I'll adjust the draft. Any other feedback?
This looks great, @522004. Very clear. Have you already reached out to the school leadership to confirm the proposed times for our visits there?
Not yet. I wanted to get the team's internal agreement first before contacting external stakeholders. I can send out the confirmation requests this afternoon.
When will the oral health sessions be? Are they on this schedule?
I've pencilled them in for the last 30 minutes of the visits to the two schools and the Northwood Community Centre, as they are larger venues. Does that work for you, @98920?
Yes, that should be fine.
This is great. Once the schedule is locked (D7), I can finalize the youth-facing materials for T7, making sure they have the correct dates and times for each location.
The rest of the schedule looks fine to me.
Sounds like a plan. Let's tentatively agree on this schedule, pending confirmation from the schools.
Update: I've heard back from both schools and the community locations. They have all confirmed the times in the revised schedule. We are good to go.

Fantastic work, @522004. That means we can make our decision. Decision D7: The weekly outreach schedule as documented in A6 is now locked in. Please make sure everyone has access to the final version.
Great, I'll update the leaflets for T7 now.
The final version of A6 is in the project folder. T6 is now complete.

threads.thread_goal: Review early pilot data, adjust approach, and plan evaluation outputs.

messages.text: Hi everyone, as part of T10 I've been monitoring the first few weeks of the pilot. I've put together a quick summary of attendance based on the data from A3. Turnout has been okay at the schools, but very low at the library.

Thanks for flagging this, @1424. I've started compiling the data for T12, and I'm seeing the same pattern. The library sessions have an average of only 2-3 attendees, while the others are closer to 10-12.
This is valuable early feedback. It seems the library is not an effective outreach location for this specific group. We should consider making a mid-pilot adjustment. What are the alternatives?
We could try moving the Wednesday session to the skate park? It's near the library, but it's where a lot of young people actually hang out. It might be better for outreach.
That's a good idea. We'd need to update the promotional materials quickly if we make that change.

I like that idea. It's responsive to what we're learning. There are safeguarding implications for a more informal outdoor setting, but our existing procedures should cover it. Let's propose this as a key adjustment for our final evaluation report (A8).

From a logistics standpoint, the skate park is feasible. It doesn't change our travel times significantly. We should document this change clearly for the evaluation, noting the reason and the outcome.
Would we do the oral health sessions at the skate park? We would need a quiet place for the one-to-one screenings.

Good point, @98920. We probably wouldn't. The skate park would be for outreach and informal chats. We can keep the more structured health and wellbeing sessions to the schools and community centres. This is another important detail for the evaluation report (A8).
So we are agreeing to change the location?

Yes, let's make a decision. Decision D8: We will make a mid-pilot adjustment to replace the library outreach session with one at the local skate park, starting next week. For the final evaluation (A8), we will highlight this change as a key lesson in responsive programming and note that different activities require different types of venues.
Confirmed. I'll update the master schedule and continue tracking the data from the new location for T12.
Understood. I'll get the updated materials ready.
Great. I will continue with T10 and report back on how the new location works out.
Ok.
Excellent. This is exactly the kind of adaptive management we need for a successful pilot. Thanks everyone for the quick and constructive input.

threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, roles and initial household targeting approach.

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the channel for our Community Food Support and Outreach Pilot! I've attached the overview doc (A1) which covers our main goals. Let's use this thread to align on the scope and how we'll approach identifying the first households. Any initial thoughts?

Thanks for setting this up. I've read A1. To make sure we're all on the same page, what does success look like after 6 weeks? Is it about the number of parcels delivered, the quality of outreach notes, or just testing if the process works? Having a clear primary goal will help us make trade-offs later.

Good to be here. The scope in A1 seems clear. For T1, I think it's important we work with our community partners to define 'vulnerable'. It could mean many things - isolated seniors, families with young children, etc. That will affect what goes in the parcels.
Hello. I am ready to start. We can create a database for the households with unique IDs for tracking. I can set that up this afternoon.
Good question. I think success is about testing the process. So, did we manage to do it safely and consistently for 6 weeks? That's probably the main thing.

Okay, 'process viability' is a good focus. Let's add 'without any safety incidents' and 'positive initial feedback from >50% of households'. That gives us something concrete to measure. What do you think?
Yes, no safety incidents is the most important part for me.

That sounds great, much clearer. Let's formalize that. D1: The pilot's success criteria are 1) consistent weekly delivery for 6 weeks, 2) zero food safety incidents, and 3) positive feedback from over half the households.
For T1, we should use a numerical scoring system for vulnerability to be objective. We can assign points for different factors.

I'd be careful with a scoring system. Our partners usually work from established relationships and professional judgement. It's less about a score and more about who they know is struggling right now. Maybe we can start with a simple criteria like 'Referred by a partner organisation' and 'Not currently receiving other food support'.

I agree with keeping it simple. The referral basis is solid and respects our partners' expertise. How many households are we aiming for? The A1 doc doesn't specify. This will impact my route planning.
I was thinking maybe 20-30? Is that too many for a pilot?
From a food prep and packing side, 30 is manageable if we have enough lead time.

Let's start with a smaller cohort, maybe 15, for the first two weeks to iron out the logistics. We can scale to 25-30 for the remaining four weeks if everything is smooth. It's less risk of failed deliveries or food waste early on.
That phased approach makes a lot of sense. It also gives us a chance to get feedback from the first group before we expand.
Ok, 15 then 30. I will prepare the tracking sheet for 30 unique IDs.

Excellent suggestion. Let's go with that. So, to confirm D2: Eligibility will be based on partner referral and not receiving other food support. We'll start with ~15 households for the first two weeks, scaling to a max of 30 for the remainder of the pilot.
Great, we're aligned on scope and targeting. I will take the action to start the conversation with our community partners based on this. That's the first part of T1.

threads.thread_goal: Design and agree on the end-to-end operational flow from surplus collection to delivery.

messages.text: Hi all, let's start thinking about the operational flow. I've drafted a simple process for T2, the surplus food collection and sorting. The idea is: 1. Collect from stores at 8am. 2. Sort into categories (fresh, ambient, chilled) by 9am. 3. Log items and check dates. 4. Move to packing area. Any initial thoughts, especially from @429831 on feasibility and @516425 on timings?

Thanks. The sorting categories are good. We need to make sure we have separate containers for each and follow the Food Safety guide (A2). We should also have a 'reject' bin for anything that looks unsafe.

Thanks for this. From my side, I need to know when the packed parcels will be ready for collection. My delivery window is tight. If packing is done by, say, 11am, I can start my routes (T4) for an afternoon delivery run. Can we work towards that?

11am is a good target. That gives us about two hours for packing after sorting. I can start drafting the packing checklist for T6. It will probably include things like: 1 bread item, 3 veg, 2 fruit, 1 protein, etc. to ensure consistency.
The checklist should be a barcode scan system. Each item type gets a barcode. The packer scans them. The system confirms the parcel is complete. This eliminates errors.
This is great progress. How will we decide the delivery schedule? Is it one day a week?

Given my existing routes, I can dedicate Tuesday and Thursday afternoons to this pilot. We could split the households between those two days. That gives us a buffer if there's an issue on one day. I'll take T4 and map out two distinct routes.

A barcode system is a bit complex for our pilot, we don't have the equipment. A simple paper checklist (A3) that the packer signs should be enough for now, as per the project constraints. We can revisit for a larger rollout.
I agree, paper is fine. I can review the draft checklist (T6) when it's ready to make sure it includes a final check on packaging integrity and temperature for chilled items.
Fine. Paper it is.
Ok, so let's lock in these decisions. It sounds like we have a plan.

To summarise and confirm: 
D3: We approve the standard process: 8am collect, 9am sort (with safety checks), 9-11am pack using a paper checklist (A3), ready for dispatch at 11am. 
D4: Deliveries will occur on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. I will own the route planning for T4. 
Does everyone agree?
Looks good. I'll finalize the process doc for T2 and draft the checklist for T6 based on this.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise safety, privacy and doorstep interaction guidelines.

messages.text: Hi team, following up on our process discussion, let's review the safety and interaction guides. I've asked @429831 to draft the Food Safety Quick Guide (A2) for T3, and I've put together a first draft of the Doorstep Script (A4) for T5. Please review and share your feedback.
Here is the draft for A2. It covers hand washing, temperature control, and checking dates. I think it has the main points. Let me know if anything is missing.
The guide looks like a good start. Should we add a line about cross-contamination, like keeping raw meat separate from other items if we ever get any?

Thanks for sharing the script draft (A4). I have a few thoughts from a delivery perspective. The question 'Are you in need of any other support?' is a bit too open and could put staff in a difficult position. Could we make it more specific, like 'We can also share a leaflet with contact numbers for other local support services, would that be helpful?' It's more manageable and still offers help.
The script should ask them to rate their wellbeing on a scale of 1 to 5. This will give us quantitative data to track over time.
That's a really helpful suggestion for the script. It keeps it non-clinical, which is a key constraint. I agree, let's change it to your proposed wording. Much better.

I don't think we can ask for a rating like that. It feels a bit too much like an assessment. The goal is a light-touch wellbeing check, not a survey. We need to keep the interaction brief and friendly.
Good point, I will add a section on preventing cross-contamination. Anything else?
Looks good otherwise. Simple and clear, which is what we need. Once that's added, I'm happy to approve it from my side.
Ok.

Great. So, let's finalize these. 
D5: We sign off on the Food Safety Guide (A2) with the added note on cross-contamination. @429831 can you upload the final version? 
D6: We agree on the final Doorstep Script (A4), using the 'offer a leaflet' wording suggested by @516425. I will update the document. 
Thanks for the excellent feedback everyone.
Will do. I'll update A2 and share it today.

threads.thread_goal: Set up tracking, labelling and logging tools before the dry run.

messages.text: For T7 and T8, I have created the templates for tracking and logging. See A5 and A6. For the labelling scheme, I propose a 6-digit alphanumeric code for each household, e.g., 4B32F1. This is fully anonymised and unique.

Thanks for drafting these. Looking at the log template A6, it seems to have a lot of columns. To keep it simple for the delivery team, could we maybe just have: Household Code, Date, Delivery Status (Success/Failed), and a small Notes field?

I agree with @44809 on simplifying A6. For the labelling code (T7), a random 6-digit code might be hard to read quickly when I'm trying to find the right parcel in the van. It's also hard to spot if one is missing from a sequence. Could we use something more structured? For example, TUE-R1-01 for Tuesday, Route 1, Stop 1. It's still anonymous but much easier to work with operationally.
I really like that structured code idea. It seems to meet the privacy needs while being practical. What does everyone else think?
A structured code is not truly random. But if it is required for operations, it is acceptable. I will update the documentation for T7.
The structured code makes sense to me. Easier to shout out if there's a problem, like 'Where is TUE-R1-01?' instead of a random number.
I will also simplify the log template A6 as requested.
Perfect. Let's make that the official decision then. D7: We will use a structured, non-random coding scheme for parcels and households, following the format DAY-ROUTE-STOP (e.g., TUE-R1-01).
Great, that will make things much smoother. Thanks @534740 for being flexible and updating the docs.

threads.thread_goal: Review dry run results and agree adjustments and next steps.

messages.text: Hi all, we've completed the one-week dry run (T10). From the operational side, things went mostly to plan. We had one issue where a batch of surplus bread was already stale on collection, which I've logged in A7. Packing took about 15 minutes longer than expected for the first batch.

Thanks for the summary. On the delivery side, the new labelling system worked perfectly. The routes were okay, but one street was closed, causing a 20-minute delay. I've also logged this in A7. The doorstep interactions felt good; the script was easy to use. Most people were just happy to get the parcel and didn't want to chat long.

The extra packing time is probably just a learning curve. We can probably speed that up next week. Regarding the stale bread, maybe we need to add a 'quality check' step right at the point of collection, not just during sorting.
I have processed the logs from A6. All 5 households were delivered successfully. There are 3 notes in the notes field. I have compiled them.
This is all really valuable feedback. It sounds like the core process works but needs a few tweaks. What does everyone think, are we ready to proceed with the full pilot next week?
Yes, adding a quality check at collection is a good idea. I can add that to the process doc.

I'd say yes, it's a 'go'. The issues we found are minor and fixable. My proposed adjustments are: 1. Add the quality check at collection point as @44809 suggested. 2. Build an extra 30 minutes of buffer time into my delivery routes to account for unexpected delays. With those changes, I'm confident we can scale up to the next group of households.
That sounds like a clear and sensible plan. Does anyone disagree with that assessment?
No, I agree. Let's go for it.
I am ready to continue.

Excellent. Then let's make it official. D8: We are 'go' for the full 6-week pilot roll-out, with two agreed process changes: 1) Add a quality check at food collection, and 2) Add a 30-minute buffer to delivery route timings.
I will now focus on the weekly monitoring for T11 and start thinking about the structure for the final report A8. Great work on the dry run, everyone!

threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, touchpoints, and overall pilot plan.

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the channel for the Cross-Channel Customer Feedback Improvement Pilot. The goal is to design and run a 6-week pilot to better capture and use customer feedback. Let's kick off by confirming the scope. I've started mapping the current process in A1, based on my initial understanding. Please review and let's align on the touchpoints to include.

Thanks for setting this up. For the insurance side, our main touchpoints are the claims hotline and the policy renewal email sequence. Both should be in scope. I've already started looking at how our current complaint codes could map to a new system for T7.

For the cellar, the primary touchpoint is the post-tour feedback form. We need to be careful about timing. The project constraints mention minimal disruption during peak hours. We should only collect feedback during the tasting portion of the tour, not during the main cellar walk-through when machinery is active.
Good point, that's a critical operational detail. Let's add that as a requirement for the cellar checklist process. Thanks.
Hello. For the help desk, we get feedback through support tickets and the post-resolution survey. Are both of those in scope?

Hi all. For membership, we have the annual survey, welcome calls for new members, and our general inquiry email. I think for the pilot we should focus on the welcome calls and the inquiry email to get more immediate feedback.
Yes, both tickets and the survey are in scope. We want to see how we can unify the data from them.
Good suggestion. Focusing on welcome calls and emails for membership seems manageable for a pilot. Let's hold off on the annual survey for now.
The project pack mentions a 30-day deadline for the pilot and report. Does that mean the pilot itself (T11) runs for ~3 weeks to leave a week for analysis and reporting?

Exactly. I'm proposing a timeline of: Week 1 for setup (tasks T1-T10), Weeks 2-4 for the pilot run (T11), and Week 5 for analysis and the final report. This fits within the 30-day constraint. Does this timeline work for everyone?
That timeline is tight but feasible from my side, as long as the checklist is simple.
Works for me.
Ok, I can make that work.
The timeline is fine for the membership team.

Great, we have alignment. To summarize the decisions:
1. The pilot will cover these touchpoints: Help Desk (tickets, survey), Membership (welcome calls, inquiry email), Insurance (claims hotline, renewal email), and Cellar (post-tour form during tasting). (D1)
2. We agree on the 30-day timeline: 1 week setup, 3 weeks pilot, 1 week reporting. (D2)
I will update the project plan accordingly.
My next step is to complete the initial touchpoint map (T1) based on this discussion and share it by EOD. Then I'll start on the unified taxonomy (T2).
Sounds good. I'll be ready to review the taxonomy when it's available.
Thanks for the summary.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise the unified feedback taxonomy and routing rules.

messages.text: Team, I've drafted the first version of the Unified Feedback Taxonomy (A2). The goal is to have a consistent set of categories for T2. Please review and provide feedback, especially on whether these categories cover the common feedback you receive.

Thanks, taking a look now. The categories 'Product Issue', 'Service Quality', and 'Billing Inquiry' map well to our existing insurance complaint codes. I'm working on the full mapping for T7. I suggest adding a sub-tag for 'Urgent' under 'Product Issue' for things that require immediate escalation.

The draft looks like a good starting point. For cellar visits, we often get feedback on the physical environment. Could we add a category for 'Facility/Venue Experience'? This would cover comments on cleanliness, safety, or ambiance. It's distinct from 'Service Quality' which is more about the staff interaction.
Good idea. An 'Urgent' flag is a great addition for routing. I'll add it.
I agree, 'Facility/Venue Experience' is a valuable addition. I'll add that category. Thanks.
I see 'Technical Issue' on the list. Should that be used for website problems, like a broken link, or is it for something else?
Yes, 'Technical Issue' is the right category for website problems, app bugs, or login issues. I'll add a few examples to the guideline in A2 to make it clearer.
This looks good. The categories cover what we hear from members. 'Membership Program Feedback' is perfect for our needs.

Okay, I've incorporated the feedback. The updated category list is now in A2. Let's talk about routing. My proposal is:
- Technical Issues -> Help Desk
- Insurance-specific -> Insurance Team
- Membership Program -> Membership Team
- Facility/Venue -> Cellar Master
- General Service/Product -> Initially to BI for triage, then routed. Does this work?
That routing logic works for insurance. We'll monitor the queue for our tags. We can track this in the Pilot Feedback Log A5, right?
Correct. Everything will be logged in A5 with owner and status.
Routing for technical issues to us is correct.
Routing facility feedback to me is fine. I'll check the log daily.
Works for the membership team.

Excellent. We have agreement. I'm marking these as decided:
1. The final list of feedback categories and tags in A2 is approved. (D3)
2. The proposed routing rules for each category are agreed upon. (D4)
I will finalize the A2 document and set up the shared log A5 tomorrow morning.
Great, I'll complete the T7 mapping against the final A2 tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Align on frontline scripts, checklists, and training approach.

messages.text: Hi all, as part of T3, I've drafted the help desk intake script for capturing feedback. You can find it in A4. I tried to keep it concise while including the consent and privacy notice. Please let me know your thoughts.

Thanks for sharing this. It looks like a solid start. For T4, I need to create a similar process for the membership team. Can we adapt this script for our welcome calls? The tone is a bit formal for us, but the core questions are good.
Absolutely. Let's make A4 a shared resource. @29126 you can add a section with a version for the membership team that has a warmer tone but captures the same structured data.
The privacy notice looks good. It's clear and covers the necessary points without being overly technical. Good job.

This is for phone calls. For the cellar visits (T6), we need something much simpler. I've created a draft checklist in A3. It's a 5-question form on a small card that guests can fill out during the wine tasting. Is this format okay, or does it need to be digital?

The paper checklist in A3 is perfect for the pilot, especially given the operational constraints. We can have someone manually enter the data into our log sheet daily. Let's confirm we'll use this during the tasting portion of every tour. (D6)
Yes, confirmed. We will hand it out with the tasting notes at the start of the tasting.
Okay, I've added our version to A4. It's ready for review.
The membership version looks good. The questions are consistent.
I've reviewed both scripts in A4. They look great. Are we ready to approve them for pilot use?
Yes, approved from my side.
Help desk script is ready.

Perfect. That's a sign-off. (D5) With the scripts and checklist finalized, the next step is training. @29126, you're leading T10. Can you schedule brief 20-minute sessions with each team next week before the pilot starts?
Yes, I will prepare the materials and send out invites for the training sessions (T10) by the end of the day.

threads.thread_goal: Set up KPI tracking, data protection rules, and dashboard expectations.

messages.text:
Hi team, let's finalize our measurement plan. I've drafted a proposal for our core KPIs and the data protection rules. Please see A7 for the data rules and my proposed KPIs for T5 below:
1. Total Feedback Volume (by channel)
2. Feedback by Category (% mix)
3. Average Time to First Response
Thoughts?

I've reviewed A7. The data protection rules are clear and align with our standard compliance requirements. Specifically, the rules on anonymizing data for reporting and the 90-day retention period for raw feedback are correct. I'm good with this. This covers T9.

The KPIs seem focused on volume and speed. Should we also try to measure the quality or impact of the feedback? For example, tracking the number of 'Actionable Insights' generated per week. It might be subjective, but it would show if the new process is actually useful, not just busy.

That's a great point. Measuring 'Actionable Insights' is a fantastic idea for value. It will be manual to start, but I can add a field in the log for us to flag these. Let's add it as a fourth KPI. Thanks for the suggestion.
The KPIs look good to me. 'Time to First Response' will be very helpful for the membership team.
I read A7. The access rules are clear. Only the assigned team can see the full customer details. That works for us.
Thanks for the quick review and confirmation on the data rules. Since everyone who has commented is aligned, can we consider the data protection and access rules in A7 approved? (D8)
Yes, approved.
Approved.

Okay, so our final KPI list is:
1. Total Feedback Volume
2. Feedback by Category
3. Avg. Time to First Response
4. Number of Actionable Insights
Is everyone happy with this list for the pilot? (D7)
Yes, this is a much better set of metrics.
Looks good.
Yes, I agree.
Great. Decisions are locked in. I will now build the simple dashboard for T5 based on these KPIs. I'll use A6 as the data source which we will populate from our central log.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on next steps and roadmap.

messages.text: Hi everyone, the 3-week pilot run (T11) is now complete. Thank you for all your hard work! I've analyzed the data and compiled the preliminary results in the Pilot Evaluation Report draft (A8). Please take a look. The key takeaway is that the unified process significantly decreased response times and increased the volume of structured feedback.
This is great to see. The data in A8 is very clear. On the insurance side, having a unified taxonomy made it much faster to identify and escalate critical issues. The process was smooth for my team.

The membership team found the new script very effective during welcome calls. We captured 4 actionable insights that have already led to improvements in our onboarding documentation. The pilot was a definite success from our perspective.

The help desk team found it easy to use the new tags. The only issue we had was some confusion between 'Technical Issue' and 'Product Issue' on a few tickets, but we sorted it out. The training was helpful.

The paper checklists worked surprisingly well. We collected over 200 of them. The main challenge was the manual data entry. If we scale this, we should look into a simple tablet-based form to automate data capture and reduce the risk of transcription errors.

threads.thread_goal: Align on MVP scope, target customers, and success metrics for the pilot.

messages.text: Team, kicking off our discussion on the MVP scope. I've put together a first draft in the 'MVP Product Vision and Scope Document'. Please take a look and share your thoughts. The goal is to get this locked in so we can move forward.

Thanks. Reading through A1 now. The vision is clear, but the target customer segment seems a bit broad. For a 30-day pilot, should we narrow our focus to 'mid-market e-commerce companies with existing data warehouses' to maximize learning and reduce onboarding friction?

Got it. Once we align on the features, I can start breaking them down into user stories for T2. Also, regarding customers, I can start building the target list for T8 as soon as we have a clear definition.
That's a good point. I was thinking a broader segment would give us more data, but maybe you're right that it's better to be focused for the pilot.
I agree with narrowing the segment. A focused approach will also make it easier to craft our GTM messaging. A single, clear value prop is much stronger than a generic one.

Exactly. It de-risks the pilot. On the feature list in A1, 'Predictive Forecasting' feels like a stretch for the MVP given the timeline. It has significant data dependencies. I'd propose we defer that and focus on the core dashboarding and reporting features. That gives us a solid foundation to build on.
From a technical standpoint, deferring 'Predictive Forecasting' is a good idea. The other features are much more feasible within 30 days on our current infrastructure.
Okay, I see the consensus building. So we're saying we should focus on the core features and not do the predictive one for now?

Yes, that seems to be the agreement. To summarize, are we ready to make a decision on these two points?
1. Defer 'Predictive Forecasting' and approve the remaining core features for the MVP.
2. Confirm the primary target segment for the pilot is 'mid-market e-commerce companies with existing data warehouses'.
That captures it perfectly. I'm in favor of both.
Works for me. This gives us a clear path forward.

Great. Thanks for summarizing, @94563. Let's formalize this. We are approving the core feature set for MVP and deferring lower-priority items like forecasting. And we are also confirming the primary target customer segment for the pilot.
Excellent. I'll update the status of T1 to reflect this and start on T2 and T8 right away. I'll have a draft of the user stories ready for review by EOD tomorrow.
I will update A1 to reflect these decisions. Thanks everyone.

threads.thread_goal: Validate technical feasibility and agree on infrastructure changes for the pilot.

messages.text: Hi team, I've completed the initial infrastructure assessment for the analytics product (T3). The summary is available in the project folder. Overall, our existing data pipelines are in good shape, but there are two potential bottlenecks: the query processing speed under concurrent user load and the data refresh latency from our primary CRM.
Thanks for this. What does 'concurrent user load' mean in this context? Are we expecting issues?

Good analysis, @123347. The CRM data latency is a key point. For the KPIs in A8, specifically customer engagement metrics, a 4-hour delay could be problematic. Can we improve the refresh rate for the pilot, or do we need to adjust the KPIs?

@22473 It means multiple users running queries at the same time. For the pilot with a small user base, it should be manageable. But if we scale, we'll need to optimize our query engine. I'd recommend we keep it as-is for the pilot to stay within the 30-day timeline.

@132848 We can increase the CRM data sync frequency to hourly. It requires a configuration change and some monitoring, but it's a low-risk change we can implement next week. That should be sufficient for the pilot KPIs.
Just to be sure, do we have all the data sources we need for the dashboard spec in A8? Or are there any gaps?
@94563 Yes, all data sources required by A8 are connected and available. The latency was the only concern, which we can address.
Deferring the query engine optimization makes sense for the pilot. We need to ensure it's captured as a key requirement for phase 2, though. Let's not lose sight of scalability.

Great. So, to confirm the path forward: 
1. The only infrastructure change in-scope for the pilot is increasing the CRM data sync frequency. All other optimizations are deferred. 
2. With that change, we confirm the current data pipelines can support the defined KPIs in A8.
Yes, that sounds right. @123347, are you good with that?
Yes, I agree with that plan. I'll formally document this for T9. So, we're agreed on the infrastructure changes for the pilot, and I can confirm the data pipelines will support the KPIs.
Perfect. I'll mark the dependencies on my side as resolved.

threads.thread_goal: Converge on pricing, subscription tiers, and discount rules.

messages.text: Team, I've completed the initial pricing analysis and have a proposal for our subscription tiers. Please review the 'Subscription Product Financial Model' (A2) for the business case and the 'Pricing and Discount Policy' draft (A5) for the specifics. The proposal is for a three-tier structure: Basic, Pro, and Enterprise, with the value metric tied to the number of data sources connected.
Thanks @132848. Looking at the financial model in A2, the cost assumptions for T4 seem a bit low. Have we factored in ongoing support costs for each tier?

The three-tier structure is standard and makes sense. My main focus is on the discount policy in A5. A 25% discretionary discount for the sales team on Enterprise deals seems high without a director-level approval. I'd suggest we cap it at 15%, with anything higher requiring VP sign-off to protect our margins.

@22473 Good catch. The current model in A2 has a simplified support cost. I've used an industry benchmark of 15% of ARR, but we can refine that. For the business case in T4, this model is primarily for strategic direction. We can build a more detailed operational budget separately.

@242297 That's a very fair point on governance. Capping the standard discount at 15% with a clear escalation path for larger discounts is a much more robust approach. I'm happy to make that change to the policy.
I like the value metric. It's simple to understand. For the pilot, are we planning to offer all three tiers or just one or two?

My recommendation is to pilot with the Pro tier only. It hits the sweet spot for our target segment and allows us to test the core value prop without the complexity of supporting the free tier or the high-touch sales process for Enterprise.
But if we only offer Pro, how do we test the other tiers?

We can still discuss the other tiers with pilot customers to get their feedback on the feature set and price points. The goal of the pilot is to validate the core product, not the entire pricing strategy. Focusing on Pro is the right move operationally.

Exactly. So, it sounds like we have a path to a decision. Shall we confirm the following?
1. We will move forward with the three-tier structure (Basic, Pro, Enterprise) for the product, but only actively pilot the Pro tier.
2. We will set the standard sales discount threshold at 15%, with VP approval required for any exceptions.
Okay, that makes sense now. I agree with both points.
Agreed.

Excellent. I'll formalize this. We have selected the final set of subscription tiers for the pilot and approved the discount thresholds and approval levels. I will update A5 accordingly and we can consider T5 complete.

threads.thread_goal: Define onboarding process and internal responsibilities for pilot customers.

messages.text: All, let's align on the operational plan for our pilot customers. I've drafted a 'Pilot Customer Onboarding Checklist' (A4) and a preliminary RACI matrix to clarify roles and responsibilities (part of T11). Please review and provide feedback on the flow and assignments.

This is great, very clear. Looking at A4, for step 3 'Initial data source connection', who is the primary point of contact for the customer if they run into issues? Is it their account manager or a technical support contact?
My team can be the first point of contact for any technical connection issues during onboarding. We should set up a dedicated alias for pilot support to streamline this.

Good question @94563. I've assigned the Customer Success Manager as 'Accountable', but @123347's suggestion is right for the 'Responsible' party. I'll update the RACI to have Tech Support as R for technical setup, with the CSM as the main relationship owner.
Who is responsible for tracking if the customer completes all the steps? Is that in the A7 tracker?

Yes, I can add columns to the 'Pilot Customer Target and Status Tracker' (A7) to mirror the checklist steps in A4. The assigned CSM for each customer will be responsible for updating the status in A7. That will give us a central view of everyone's progress.

The process looks solid. I'd suggest adding one final step to the checklist: 'Step 6: Schedule 30-day check-in to review value and gather feedback'. This ensures we have a formal loop for T12 and reinforces our partnership with the pilot customers.
Excellent addition, @132848. That closes the loop perfectly. I'll add that to A4. Any other comments or are we ready to approve this process?
Looks good to me.
I'm good with it. The ownership is clear now.

Great. Then let's make it official. We approve the onboarding checklist (A4) with the assigned owners for each step as discussed. I will publish the final version and the updated RACI for T11 by end of day.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on next-phase roadmap.

messages.text: Hi team, the 30-day pilot has concluded and I've gathered the initial performance data. The numbers are in line with the KPIs we set out to track in T10. You can see the raw data in the project folder. Let's discuss what this means for our next steps.

Thanks for sharing the data. I've cross-referenced it with the qualitative feedback from the customer check-ins. The key takeaway for me is that while adoption of the core dashboarding was high (85% MAU), the usage of 'custom report builder' was very low (<10%). Customers said it was 'confusing' and 'too complex'. This suggests our core value is in the pre-built dashboards, and the self-serve tooling needs a rethink.

That aligns with what the CSM team heard. Customers love the insights but don't want to spend time building reports. They'd rather have more pre-configured dashboards for specific use cases, like marketing campaign analysis or inventory tracking. The demand is there, but they want it to be more turnkey.

This is valuable feedback. I'm capturing these points as key learnings. So for the next-phase roadmap (T12), it sounds like we should prioritize building out a library of dashboard templates over improving the custom builder.
So we shouldn't expand the pilot yet? I thought the numbers were good.

From an infrastructure perspective, the platform was stable throughout the pilot. No performance issues were reported, even during peak usage. We are ready to support more users whenever the product is ready.

The engagement numbers are good, which validates the core problem we're solving. But the feedback on the custom builder is a significant product gap. If we expand now, we risk higher churn. I propose we don't expand yet, but instead we iterate. Let's run another 4-week cycle with the same pilot customers, replace the custom builder with 3-4 high-value dashboard templates based on their feedback, and measure the change in satisfaction and usage.

I strongly support that 'iterate' approach. It's customer-centric and reduces risk. We can position it to the pilot customers as a direct response to their feedback, which will strengthen the relationship.
That sounds like a clear plan. So the decision is to iterate on the product based on feedback before considering expansion.
Okay, I understand now. The feedback is more important than just the top-level metrics. So we are agreeing to iterate on the product, not expand or pause. I will make that the official decision.
Perfect. The data from the KPI dashboard (A8) was crucial here. This gives us a clear focus for the next iteration.
Great. My next step will be to consolidate all these learnings and draft the roadmap proposal for this next iteration phase, as per T12. I'll share a draft by the end of the week.

            "speaker_id": 22473,
            "reply_to": null,
            "text": "Hi team, the 30-day pilot has concluded and I've gathered the initial performance data. The numbers are in line with the KPIs we set out to track in T10. You can see the raw data in the project folder. Let's discuss what this means for our next steps.",

            "speaker_id": 132848,
            "reply_to": "M51",
            "text": "Thanks for sharing the data. I've cross-referenced it with the qualitative feedback from the customer check-ins. The key takeaway for me is that while adoption of the core dashboarding was high (85% MAU), the usage of 'custom report builder' was very low (<10%). Customers said it was 'confusing' and 'too complex'. This suggests our core value is in the pre-built dashboards, and the self-serve tooling needs a rethink.",
            "mentions": [],
            "artifact_refs": [],
            "decision_refs": [],
            "reactions": [
              {
                "emoji": "bulb",
                "count": 2
              }
            ]
          },

            "msg_id": "M53",
            "speaker_id": 242297,
            "reply_to": "M52",
            "text": "That aligns with what the CSM team heard. Customers love the insights but don't want to spend time building reports. They'd rather have more pre-configured dashboards for specific use cases, like marketing campaign analysis or inventory tracking. The demand is there, but they want it to be more turnkey.",
            "mentions": [],
            "artifact_refs": [],
            "decision_refs": [],
            "reactions": [

                "emoji": "+1",
                "count": 1

            "reply_to": "M51",
            "text": "This is valuable feedback. I'm capturing these points as key learnings. So for the next-phase roadmap (T12), it sounds like we should prioritize building out a library of dashboard templates over improving the custom builder.",

            "artifact_refs": [
              "T12"

            "decision_refs": [],
            "reactions": []
          },
